hypothesis: A nearly constant-height roof-only input can fail before RANSAC because the strict greater-than 25th-height-quantile filter excludes every equal-height point. Retaining such points while preserving normal, curvature, slope and support checks may recover that bounded input class.

evidence.observation: Real inputs succeed 14/14 with CD 1.2386472949634142; synthetic inputs succeed 12/16 with CD 0.42782936796658655. Aggregate scores do not identify a specific geometry correction.
Topology passes equal successful cases (14 real and 12 synthetic); no evidence here motivates changing mesh assembly.

All four listed failures report No roof plane supported. No source points or case-specific causes were inspected; constant-height filtering is a code-supported hypothesis, not a confirmed explanation of those failures.
Observed surface mismatches are present but do not establish a supported footprint or plane-domain replacement from these permitted inputs alone.
For exactly constant z, z > quantile(z, 0.25) is false for all points, so roof candidates are empty regardless of valid horizontal normals.

change: Bypass only the height-quantile gate when the total input z range is within 32 machine epsilons scaled by maximum absolute z. Keep normal/curvature filtering, RANSAC support, plane selection, completion labels, CLI and run interface unchanged. No building IDs, GT, data or evaluator changes.
expected_effect: Potentially allow supported exactly planar horizontal scans to reach plane fitting; nonconstant-height inputs retain the prior height filter. Performance is unmeasured and the four failures are not claimed resolved.
regression_risks: A constant-height ground-only scan remains indistinguishable from a roof-only scan without terrain evidence; the existing provisional base warning remains necessary.
A roof-only constant-height scan may produce zero-height walls/base and invalid solid topology because full building height is unobserved; this proposal addresses candidate exclusion only.
Existing minimum support, triangle-area and normal-estimation constraints can still prevent a plane from being fitted.
At extremely large absolute z coordinates, the machine-precision-scaled gate can admit a very thin height range.
